title: Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
content:
Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents. The startup’s new always-on “Teammates” can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use.
Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
Like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet, Perplexity’s Teammates can perform an array of tasks while running 24/7.
Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer, an AI system that can deploy agents on your device to complete tasks. But Perplexity says Teammates “build on top” of Computer by offering the ability to collaborate and complete “ongoing, large-scale work.” You can assign each Teammate different jobs that they can perform simultaneously — much like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet. Perplexity’s take on the feature is much more expensive, however, as it requires a subscription to its $200 / month Max plan.
Perplexity notes that you can keep tabs on Teammates’ progress through individual threads in the Perplexity app, as well as interact with them in Slack. “Over time, we envision every org having hundreds of teammates working for each person,” Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas says on X.

report.summary: Perplexity launched Teammates, always-on AI work agents that handle multiple roles, integrate with its Computer system, and require its $200/month Max plan.
report.background: Perplexity built its reputation on AI-powered search and is now pushing into workplace productivity, where OpenAI and Anthropic are racing to turn chatbots into autonomous agents. The shift reflects growing enterprise demand for AI that can execute ongoing tasks, retain context, and work across tools rather than answer one-off prompts. Perplexity’s Teammates build on its Computer system, which deploys agents on a user’s device, and add collaboration, memory, and large-scale work capabilities. The launch puts Perplexity in direct competition with OpenAI’s Dots and Anthropic’s Claude Duet, but at a premium price through its $200-per-month Max plan. The company is betting that always-on, role-specific agents will become a core way organizations delegate work.
key_points: Teammates are always-on AI agents that can take on multiple roles inside a workspace. Users can assign different jobs to different Teammates and run them simultaneously, then monitor progress through individual threads in the Perplexity app or interact with them in Slack.

The agents build on Perplexity Computer, which deploys AI agents on a user’s device to complete tasks. Teammates add collaboration and memory, pulling existing projects, skills, and context from Perplexity tools so they can handle ongoing, large-scale work rather than isolated requests.

Perplexity positions Teammates against OpenAI’s Dots and Anthropic’s Claude Duet, two similar work-focused agent offerings. The key difference is pricing: Teammates require the $200-per-month Max plan, making Perplexity’s take significantly more expensive than some rival options.

CEO Aravind Srinivas says Perplexity envisions organizations eventually having hundreds of Teammates working for each person. That ambition signals a shift from AI as a single assistant to fleets of specialized agents handling parallel workflows across a company.
report.impact: Perplexity’s move validates the industry’s shift from conversational AI to always-on, role-based agents that can execute work across apps and memory. For the AI industry, competition will increasingly center on autonomy, context retention, integrations, and pricing rather than raw model quality alone. Developers may see more demand for agent orchestration, scheduling, and Slack-style workplace integrations, though Perplexity has not detailed a public developer platform. For regular users, Teammates remain gated behind a $200 monthly plan, limiting access to high-spending professionals and teams. The bigger question is reliability: always-on agents must handle permissions, errors, and long-running tasks without creating costly mistakes.
report.tools: Watch Perplexity Teammates and Perplexity Computer, plus rivals OpenAI Dots and Anthropic Claude Duet. For hands-on open-source experimentation, try Microsoft AutoGen for multi-agent orchestration, CrewAI for role-based agent teams, LangGraph for stateful workflows, and OpenHands for coding agents. These projects let developers prototype always-on, role-specific agents and compare memory, scheduling, and workplace integrations.
